answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/klarna/supplementary-purchase-data, the November capture documents a public preview requiring API header 2025-11-17.preview or a later preview header, and Klarna-only supplementary data for eight listed verticals. A server-side PaymentIntent create, update or confirm carries payment_method_options.klarna.supplementary_purchase_data; arrays can contain multiple entries and verticals, with replacement per updated vertical, omitted verticals preserved, and empty strings clearing one or all (new raw lines 9-59,349-416). Well-formed data is accepted without validation feedback about improved outcomes, and fees do not change. The May guide establishes the same behavior (old raw lines 8-58,564-705). The mapped source-stripe-klarna-supplementary-data.md correctly summarizes those boundaries (source lines 13-29). Neither capture establishes an actual approval, fraud result, or successful payment.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/klarna/supplementary-purchase-data, the substantive prose, preview gate, eight verticals and PaymentIntent update semantics are unchanged (old raw lines 8-58,564-705; new raw lines 9-59,349-416). The visible delta is mainly presentation and example integration: the May Node SDK examples explicitly use payment_method_types ['klarna'], while November curl examples enable automatic_payment_methods; both are server-side secret-key examples, and this does not prove Klarna eligibility, client behavior or payment success (old raw lines 60-115; new raw lines 61-84). Preserve May example provenance and November syntax separately. The linked field schemas are outside these captures, and source-stripe-klarna-supplementary-data.md remains substantively accurate; its header wording can be tightened to mention later preview versions (source line 17). The related BNPL concept has no conflicting supplementary-data rule.
